messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — I'm starting a short RFC follow-up: proposal to create 'service corridors' for ownership (hotpath, enrichment, controlplane). Trying to capture tradeoffs and migration guardrails.
kevin: +1, we need a clear rollback story. curious how this differs from previous 'slice' work.
maria.g: Good call. Difference is explicit per-corridor runtime SLA and a small shim layer for backward compat during cutover. Goal: reduce cross-team churn when changing hotpath logic.
ida: Can you sketch the shim?
maria.g: idea: lightweight adapter that translates legacy facade -> new corridor API. config in front router toggles routing. Example config: 
```
route: /v1/generate
pipeline: legacy-facade | adapter-corridor-hotpath
flags:
  corridor_enabled: tenantA,tenantB
```
kevin: That looks fine. How do we handle KV cache ownership? Hotpath needs low-latency local cache, enrichment can be eventual.
maria.g: Hotpath gets dedicated KV instance colocated with workers. Enrichment reads from shared read-replica. We'll add cache-coherence validator in rollout tests.
sam: Testing plan? Need smoke + perf + e2e. Also cost estimate: dedicated KV for hotpath might bump infra.
ida: For rollouts, suggest canary by tenant + traffic shadowing for 48-72h, with automatic fallback if p50 latency increases >10% or error rate >0.5%.
kevin: Agree. Add automatic model-fallback path too (so if new corridor OOMs, route to legacy model variant).
infra-bot: deploy triggered: ci/corridor-adapter-canary -> staging at 2026-03-20T14:05:12Z
maria.g: Ops checklist draft: 1) adapter feature flag gate 2) KV provision script 3) canary config per-tenant 4) observability dashboards (latency, errors, cost) 5) abort plan commands
kevin: Suggest we also add 'safety net' quota guard so runaway batching doesn't spike token costs.
sam: +1 on quota guard. Also add a minimal perf harness to replay production-ish traces.
ida: One concern — ownership handoffs. Who owns the adapter? I'd prefer Platform (infra) to own the runtime shim; product teams own corridor logic.
maria.g: That matches intent. I'll update RFC notes: Platform team owns adapter & rollout infra; corridor teams own APIs and tests.
kevin: Timeline?
maria.g: Proposal: prototype week 1, internal canary week 2, broad canary week 3-4, opt-in tenants by end of month 2.
sam: Sounds reasonable. Please add a short rollback playbook to the RFC.
maria.g: Will do. I'll post updated RFC doc and link it here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
